evidence: AST-based import graph analysis across all Python files found zero strongly-connected cycles among project package roots (overlays/, kernels/, tests/, benchmarks/, campaign-2026-08/, quanttrio-tp4-dcp2/, aeon-crossnode-graphs/, dspark-training/, gates/, platform/), so there are no circular dependency cycles in the project's own code.

The codebase has no project-level dependency manifest (no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.py, poetry.lock, or package-lock.json). Dependencies are inherited from the pinned Docker base images and the MANIFEST.json overlay system, which is appropriate for a runtime overlay kit but makes local development dependency auditing harder.

Production image pinning is explicit: images/vllm-b12x.Dockerfile pins b12x to commit 334a2d75d166becea0aa640b402d521ea0a290eb and nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.0; MANIFEST.json records md5s and provenance for every overlay.

Two Dockerfiles are byte-identical: aeon-crossnode-graphs/Dockerfile and platform/Dockerfile both build the AEON 0.27.1 base + b12x@334a2d75 and copy overlays into site-packages. Keeping both means any future dependency pin edit must be made in two places.

Dependency version drift exists between build contexts: campaign-2026-08/images/Dockerfile force-reinstalls b12x from ref 36bce2c15 and nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2 on top of the production vllm-b12x:v0.27.0-pinned image (which already pins b12x@334a2d75 and cutlass-dsl 4.6.0). This means the campaign image and production image can ship different sparse-MLA/cutlass-dsl behavior.

Third-party `regex` is imported as `re` in overlays/vllm/engine/arg_utils.py and overlays/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py. This adds an implicit extra dependency beyond the Python standard library `re` module, and because the repo has no manifest the requirement is not visible to a reader or installer.

dependency_health.dimension_character: The project is a Docker-based runtime overlay kit, so its dependency story is intentionally image-level rather than manifest-driven. Pinning is generally explicit and there are no circular import cycles, but there is real dependency drift between the production image, the campaign image, and the legacy/v0.27 experimental images, plus an implicit third-party `regex` dependency and a duplicated Dockerfile.
dependency_health.score_rationale: A score of 70.0 reflects solid baseline health: no cycles, clear image-level pinning for production, and domain-appropriate heavy dependencies. The score is held below 80 by cross-context pin drift, a duplicated Dockerfile declaration, and the absence of any project-level dependency manifest that would make the implicit `regex` requirement discoverable.

issues.summary: aeon-crossnode-graphs/Dockerfile and platform/Dockerfile are byte-identical, creating a maintenance hazard for dependency pins.
evidence: diff -q reports no differences between the two files.
Both files use FROM ghcr.io/aeon-7/aeon-vllm-ultimate:2026-08-16-v0.27.1, ARG B12X_REF=334a2d75d166becea0aa640b402d521ea0a290eb, and COPY overlays/ into /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/.
issues.suggestion: Delete one Dockerfile and reference the other from both locations, or move the shared image definition to a single file (e.g., images/glm52-spark-platform.Dockerfile) and have both aeon-crossnode-graphs/ and platform/ build from it.

issues.summary: Campaign/legacy build contexts override production b12x and cutlass-dsl pins without a visible compatibility guard.
evidence: campaign-2026-08/images/Dockerfile starts from vllm-b12x:v0.27.0-pinned (above pins) but then force-reinstalls b12x@36bce2c15 and nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2.
quanttrio-tp4-dcp2/v027/Dockerfile.deepgemm-fix uses vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.0-aarch64 rather than the production vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.0 tag.
issues.suggestion: Document each pin override in its build context README and add an image-build assertion that prints/verifies the installed versions of b12x and nvidia-cutlass-dsl; align pins to production unless an experiment specifically requires a newer version.

issues.summary: Overlay files import the third-party `regex` package as `re`, but the repo has no manifest declaring it.
evidence: No requirements.txt/pyproject.toml exists to record `regex` as a dependency, so it is not obvious whether the package is provided by the base image or an accidental extra.
issues.suggestion: If stdlib `re` suffices, replace `import regex as re` with `import re`; otherwise add a dependency note (e.g., in README.md or a requirements.txt) and a runtime import guard that falls back to stdlib `re` when `regex` is unavailable.

root_causes: The repo was formed by folding three independent repositories together and keeping them as in-place archives, so dependency declarations were copied rather than unified.
The overlay-first deployment model pushes dependency ownership into Docker images, so there is no single project manifest to expose version drift or implicit packages.
possible_false_positives: co-occurring dataclasses and pydantic in vLLM config overlay files is an upstream vLLM pattern, not a project-level duplicate-library choice.
Stdlib `re` is never imported alongside `regex` in the same file, so the two are not competing in the same module.

add.description: Production dependencies are pinned inside Dockerfiles and base image tags (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.0, b12x commit ref, nvidia-cutlass-dsl version) rather than in a Python package manifest. This matches the overlay runtime model and gives reproducible fleet images, but it also means there is no single local dependency file to audit.

AST-based SCC analysis found no circular import cycles across project package roots. Dependency direction is clean because most modules are vLLM overlays that import upstream vllm/torch rather than each other.
